f.title: Treat journals read by prescribers with scientific content as relevant for national literature searching
f.statement: For literature searching, a journal is considered relevant if its audience includes persons authorised to prescribe medicines and its content is scientifically relevant; journals included in university library collections would normally be considered scientifically relevant. Inadequate national literature searching is listed as a typical inspection deviation.
f.clause: Examples of typical deviations - Literature searching
f.applicability: Literature searching, including national literature searching, by MAHs inspected by the Danish Medicines Agency
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote: A journal is considered relevant if its audience includes persons who are authorised to prescribe medicines and its content is scientifically relevant. Journals included in university library collections would normally be considered as scientifically relevant.
rows.location: Examples of typical deviations - Literature searching
rows.review_note: Review: only normative content on the page; the rest describes DKMA's risk-based inspection selection and lists typical deviations (findings), which state no duty in normative wording and are not curated. Double-check: definition proven; level Recommended as an authority Q&A interpretation; below 90 because the page is dated 2019 and the definition is an interpretation rather than a stated duty.
